transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, doc. Um, well, I came in because I just feel worn out almost every single day. Like, even if I get a full night's sleep, my body and my head are just completely dragging when I have to get up for my cashier shift. I work over at the grocery store, and man, the registers there are so old the scanners barely work half the time. Just yesterday this lady got so mad at me because her coupon wouldn't scan, but it's like, I don't build the machines, you know? The receipt paper jammed right after that, too, took me ten minutes to fix it. But, uh, yeah... anyway, I just can't seem to wake up feeling rested no matter what I do.
Do you often wake up feeling unrefreshed, like your sleep didn't really help you rest, even if you slept long enough?

Yeah, exactly. It's like... most nights I'll get into bed, and I'm exhausted, you know? But then I just lie there. My brain starts going over all the bills I have to pay, my work schedule for the week, wondering if everyone at home is doing okay. My brother actually just got a new dog, a little terrier mix, and I swear that thing barks at every single leaf that blows past the window. He brought it over last weekend and it chewed up my favorite pair of slippers. The brown leather ones, I got them on sale at the mall like three years ago. Anyway, yeah, even when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up feeling like my brain never really turned off or settled down. It's just exhausting.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with family?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel depressed or anything like that. I still like doing my usual stuff, you know? Like, I still watch the game on Sundays. Though, honestly, the team has been doing so terrible this season, it's almost hard to watch. My buddy Dave came over last week to watch the game, and he brought this dip, right? It was supposed to be a seven-layer dip, but I swear it was just sour cream and some sad-looking beans. And he spilled it on my rug. I spent like an hour trying to scrub it out with this carpet cleaner I bought off an infomercial. It actually worked pretty well, surprisingly. But yeah, no, I don't feel hopeless or anything. Just tired, mostly.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down, depressed, or lost interest in most activities for most of the day, more days than not?

No, like I said, I don't feel depressed or down. I still enjoy stuff. It's just... I'm so tired. And honestly, it doesn't help that the weather's been so weird lately. Like, one day it's freezing, and the next day I'm sweating in my jacket waiting for the bus. The bus system in this city is a total joke, by the way. I was waiting for the 42 the other day, and it just drove right past me. Splashed a puddle all over my jeans. I had to go to work with wet ankles, which is just the worst feeling, standing at a register for eight hours with damp socks. But no, to answer your question, I'm not feeling depressed or losing interest in things. Just... yeah, just worn out.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep during the night?

Well, yeah, like I was saying earlier, I definitely have trouble falling asleep. My brain just won't shut up. But staying asleep... I don't know, once I'm finally out, I think I stay asleep okay. Unless my neighbor decides to start his motorcycle at 3 AM again. I swear, that guy has zero respect for anyone else on the street. It's this loud, obnoxious chopper thing, and he just sits in his driveway revving it. I talked to the landlord about it, but he's practically useless. Took him three weeks just to fix the leaky faucet in my bathroom. I ended up having to put a bucket under it, and the sound of the dripping was driving me crazy. Drip... drip... drip... right when I was trying to sleep. But yeah, falling asleep is the main issue, not really waking up in the middle of the night, unless there's a racket outside.
Do you find yourself feeling excessively sleepy during the day, even after a full night’s sleep?

Yeah, that's actually exactly why I came in. I just feel so worn out almost every day. Like, even if I do manage to get a full night's sleep—assuming the motorcycle guy is quiet—I still wake up and my body and head are just dragging. Getting up for my cashier shift feels like pulling teeth. And speaking of my shift, they just changed the schedule again without telling anyone. My manager, Brenda, she's always doing that. She'll post the new schedule on a Thursday for the next week, but then she'll go in with a red pen on Friday and change it. It's so frustrating because I'll make plans, you know? Like I was supposed to go to my cousin's barbecue last weekend, and I had to cancel last minute because Brenda decided she needed me on register four. And register four is the worst one because the scanner is sticky from when some kid spilled a soda on it like three months ago. They never cleaned it properly. But yeah, I'm just exhausted all the time during the day, no matter what.
Do you often wake up feeling like you didn’t really sleep at all, even if you were in bed for a long time?

Yeah, pretty much every morning. I'll get into bed feeling totally wiped out, but then my brain just kicks into overdrive. I'll lie there for hours, just going over my bills, worrying about my work schedule—like I said about Brenda—and just stressing if everyone in my family is okay. And honestly, even when I do finally drift off, I wake up feeling like I never really settled down at all. It's like my brain was running a marathon while my body was just lying there. Speaking of marathons, did you know they shut down Main Street last Sunday for that 10K? It was a nightmare trying to get to the grocery store. I had to detour all the way down Elm, and of course, there was construction on Elm. They've been tearing up that road for what feels like a year. I don't even know what they're fixing anymore. Just orange cones everywhere, and nobody actually working when you drive by. But yeah, waking up is rough. I never feel rested.
Even when you are able to fall asleep and stay asleep, do you still wake up feeling like you haven't truly rested?

Yeah, I mean, I think I just said that, but yeah. It's exactly like that. Like, I get into bed and I'm so tired, my eyes are burning, but then the second my head hits the pillow, it's just... bam. Bills, Brenda and her stupid red pen, worrying if my mom remembered to lock her back door because there was that string of break-ins over in West End last month. Did you hear about that? They were stealing catalytic converters right out of people's driveways. My buddy Dave, he drives an old Honda, and he woke up one morning, started his car, and it sounded like a tractor. Turns out they sawed the thing right off. Cost him like eight hundred bucks to replace, and his insurance wouldn't even cover the whole thing because of some fine print about aftermarket parts. It's such a scam, insurance. You pay them every month and then when you actually need them, they find a loophole. But anyway, yeah, even if I don't wake up in the middle of the night, when my alarm goes off, I feel like I didn't even sleep. Like my brain was just spinning the whole time.
Even when you sleep through the night without waking up, do you still wake up feeling unrested or like your sleep wasn’t restful?

Yeah, doc, I mean... I feel like we're going in circles here a bit. I literally just told you that. Yes, even if I sleep straight through, I wake up feeling like garbage. It's like my brain never shuts off. Honestly, it's making me so irritable, especially at work. Like yesterday, this lady came through my line—register four, of course, with the sticky scanner—and she had a cart absolutely full of cat food. Just cans and cans of it. And she wanted me to bag them in a very specific way, like three cans to a bag, double-bagged, because she said her cloth bags would rip. I tried telling her the plastic bags are pretty sturdy now, but she wasn't having it. And she kept pulling out these crumpled coupons from like, 2019. I had to call Brenda over to override the system, and you know how much I love dealing with Brenda. But yeah, to answer your question again, no matter how long I'm out, I never feel rested.
Would you say that your sleep feels unrefreshing most of the time, even when you don’t have any interruptions during the night?

Look, doc... are you messing with me? I feel like I'm on some hidden camera show or something. How many times are you gonna ask me the exact same thing? Yes. Yes, my sleep is unrefreshing. Like I've been saying, most nights I get in bed totally exhausted, but then I'm just lying there, staring at the ceiling, going over my bills, stressing about my schedule, worrying if everyone at home is alright. And then, like I said three times now, even when I do finally manage to sleep, I wake up feeling like I never settled down at all. It's like I'm more tired waking up than when I went to sleep. 

Honestly, it reminds me of this time I tried to fix my lawnmower. I spent like four hours yanking on the pull cord, taking the spark plug out, cleaning the carburetor—which, by the way, is a total pain on those old Briggs & Stratton engines. The manual makes it look so easy, just "unscrew this and wipe that," but it's never like that. You always end up with grease under your fingernails for a week. Anyway, I spent all afternoon on it, sweating in the sun, and at the end of the day, the stupid thing still wouldn't start. I put in all that effort and got absolutely nowhere. That's exactly what my sleep feels like. Just a lot of work for zero payoff. But yeah, to answer your question for the fourth time, yes, my sleep is completely unrefreshing.
